title: Bangladesh Beat Australia at Home in an ODI for the First Time. The Margin Was 86 Runs.
excerpt: Mosaddek Hossain's unbeaten 86 and Nahid Rana's four-wicket haul gave Bangladesh a dominant DLS victory in Dhaka, ending a decades-long wait for a home ODI win against Australia.
body:
For twenty-one years, Bangladesh had tried to beat Australia in a home One-Day International. Twenty-one years of close calls and lopsided scorecards. On Tuesday in Mirpur, at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium, the wait ended — and it was not close.

Bangladesh crushed Australia by 86 runs via the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method in the first ODI of the three-match series. It was a victory built on discipline with the bat, ferocity with the ball, and a middle-order innings from Mosaddek Hossain that will be remembered in Dhaka for a long time.

## Mosaddek's Masterclass

Bangladesh's innings had wobbled early. Saif Hassan fell for a duck, and though Tanzid Hasan Tamim and Najmul Hossain Shanto both struck half-centuries to stabilize the top order, wickets kept falling at inconvenient moments. At 140 for 4, the hosts needed someone to convert a promising position into an imposing total.

Mosaddek did exactly that. Coming in at number six, he played with calm authority, rotating strike when needed, punishing anything short or full. His unbeaten 86 off 70 balls — the innings of the match by any measure — carried Bangladesh from a middling position to a formidable 284 for 8 off their 50 overs. It was the kind of knock that separates match-winners from run-scorers.

Tanzid's 50 at the top and Shanto's patient contribution in the middle overs had laid the groundwork. Taskin Ahmed's cameo at the death added useful runs. But this was Mosaddek's day.

## Nahid Rana's Fury

If the batting was clinical, the bowling was devastating. Australia's reply disintegrated from the very first ball. Matthew Short fell on the first delivery of the innings. Two balls into his second over, Nahid Rana had Marnus Labuschagne caught as well. Australia were 2 for 2.

Nahid, the fast bowler who has rapidly become one of the most exciting quicks in world cricket, finished with figures of 4 for 41 from his 10 overs. His pace was consistently in the high 140s, his lengths were probing, and his aggression was relentless. This was an older, wiser version of the bowler who had terrorized Josh Inglis in Pakistan just weeks earlier — and this time, he had the scoreboard on his side.

Australia never recovered from the early collapse. Josh Inglis, leading the side in the absence of the injured Mitchell Marsh, managed 21 before falling to a rash shot. Cooper Connolly offered brief resistance with 31, and Alex Carey contributed 25. Only Cameron Green, batting with the tail, showed genuine fight — his unbeaten 52 off 66 balls was the lone innings of substance, but it was far too late.

At 191 for 9 in 42.2 overs, lightning forced play to be abandoned. The DLS par score was 198. Bangladesh won by 86 runs.

## What This Means for Bangladesh Cricket

The significance cannot be overstated. Bangladesh had beaten Australia in Tests — the famous 2017 Dhaka victory, powered by Shakib Al Hasan's ten-wicket match haul, remains one of the great upsets in Test history. But in the shorter format, at home, Australia had always found a way.

This was not a scrappy, last-ball escape. This was comprehensive. Bangladesh outplayed Australia in all three departments of the game. The bowling attack, led by Nahid and supported by the wily Mustafizur Rahman and the spin of Mehidy Hasan Miraz, made Australia's lineup look ordinary.

For the Bangladeshi diaspora — spread across the United States, the United Kingdom, and the Middle East — this is the kind of result that transcends cricket. It is a reminder that Bangladesh is no longer the team other nations expect to roll over. The Tigers are competitive, consistent, and on any given day, capable of beating anyone.

The second ODI will be played on Thursday in Dhaka. If Nahid Rana is in the same mood, Australia will need a significantly better plan.

## Match Summary

**Bangladesh** 284/8 (50 overs) — Mosaddek Hossain 86* (70), Tanzid Hasan Tamim 50, Najmul Hossain Shanto 50

**Australia** 191/9 (42.2 overs) — Cameron Green 52* (66); Nahid Rana 4/41, Nathan Ellis 3/38

**Result:** Bangladesh won by 86 runs (DLS method)

**Player of the Match:** Mosaddek Hossain
